# The story

Every Saturday when she was a girl, my grandmother walked from her village to the
market in Dessie. She left before dawn with her mother, carrying a basket of eggs
and two clay jars of butter wrapped in false-banana leaves, and the road took
almost three hours, down through the eucalyptus and across a stream she was
afraid of.

At the market she was allowed to bargain for one thing herself. Most weeks it was
coffee beans. She liked the smell of the coffee sellers' corner more than the
noise of the cattle side, and the coffee women let her taste a little roasted
bean.

On the walk home, tired, she would ask how much further. Her mother always
answered the same way: "Kes be kes, enqulal be egru yihedal" - little by little,
an egg will walk on its own legs. Patience, and the egg grows legs.

Today my grandmother roasts coffee for all of us on Sundays, and when one of us
complains that something is taking too long, she says it to us, and laughs.
